mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts rate exceeding 2,000,000 units signals robust consumer confidence and residential construction demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through increased consumer spending and corporate investment.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 2000.0, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate and increases in nonfarm payrolls indicate a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS does not produce a statistically significant positive return (p>0.05) in the S&P 500 over 20 days when both series move in the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), higher interest rates and persistent inflation pressure reduce corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales index (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which is a leading indicator of corporate revenue growth and earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The RSAFS trend does not correlate with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index above 120.0 signals robust manufacturing activity, which typically precedes higher corporate profits and positive equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO exceeds 120.0, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery regime (UNRATE below 5.0% and PAYEMS growth above 100k), strong employment conditions boost consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 100k, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% indicates persistent inflation, which typically leads to delayed monetary policy easing and higher real interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL is above 3.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
